key_insight: Combining low-cost sparse IMUs with Project Aria egocentric vision yields a hybrid wearable (RoSHI) that can recover full 3D human pose and body shape in a metric global coordinate frame, enabling robust, portable capture of long-horizon interactions in the wild.
problem_solved: Addresses the trade-offs in collecting human interaction data for robot learning—portability, robustness to occlusion, and global spatial consistency—by producing globally-referenced, full-body pose and shape from egocentric perception.
method: Hardware fusion: a lightweight wearable that pairs Project Aria glasses with a few low-cost IMUs to capture complementary visual and inertial signals.
Sensor-level alignment: calibrates and registers egocentric camera frames and IMU measurements into a shared metric global coordinate frame.
Model-level fusion: a learning-based sensor-fusion pipeline that integrates sparse inertial cues and egocentric visual features to estimate long-horizon 3D pose and body shape robust to occlusions.
impact: Enables scalable, in-the-wild collection of metrically-consistent human behavior datasets for robot learning, imitation, and simulation, reducing reliance on fixed capture studios and improving real-world generalization.

paper_title: RoSHI: A Versatile Robot-oriented Suit for Human Data In-the-Wild
paper_authors: Wenjing Margaret Mao, Jefferson Ng, Luyang Hu, Daniel Gehrig, Antonio Loquercio
